summary: When the project has an approved Process Policy, each backlog review round records its path, revision and source hash, the pin a Delivery takes at scope approval, as the policy in force when the round is written: `backlog_compile.py init`, `stub-epic` and `begin-revision` write their rounds with it, and `check` pins a draft round the Product Owner writes the first time it sees it, reporting it in `pinned_reviews`, never an approved round. `backlog_compile.py approve` records the same pin in `backlog.md` and refuses, before any write, a review it approves whose round records another policy, naming the remedy: rerun the review in a new round under the current policy, or restore the policy it ran under. An earlier round keeps its own pin, so a backlog revision and its reviews outside any Delivery name the process switch values they ran under. The pin follows `approved_at_utc` once approved and sits inside the notes' source and package hashes. After approval it is a record and is never compared: a later policy revision leaves the approved backlog current, a round approved earlier keeps its own pin, and `begin-revision` drops the pin from the new draft root until its own approval. A round written while the policy is a draft records nothing and is pinned by the first check after the policy's approval. A draft or invalid policy refuses a new approval before any write; re-approving an unchanged approved backlog is unaffected. Without a policy nothing is recorded, and a new golden all-default approval run proves every backlog file the approval writes byte-identical to the previous release apart from #306's legacy story fix. The `story_size_budget` instructions now leave the policy revision to that record and keep only the limits in an epic review's Slicing evidence.
